title: Alphabet's $4 Trillion Empire: 4 Engineers' Departure Shocks Market #shorts
description: A $4 trillion tech titan faces a crisis as 4 key engineers depart, wiping 5% off market value. Gemini 3.5 Pro development lags, even as capital expenditures soar to $200 billion. Can they maintain supremacy? #TechIndustry #Alphabet #Engineering #BusinessNews #AI

top_comments.author: @TheOkie13
top_comments.text: Good, and i need to de google my phone to before the OS lockdown.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Totally get the urgency. Moving away before the next update drops means picking between convenience and control — you’ll likely end up sideloading, swapping services, and tweaking a lot more yourself. It’s a hassle up front but gives you way more say over what runs on your phone. What’s driving it most for you — keeping data private, avoiding restrictions, or just wanting a phone that’s actually yours?

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Totally. It’s like putting all the eggs in one basket, then strapping rockets to it. One crack and the whole thing goes. Are you seeing that most in tech stacks or in markets?

top_comments.author: @MountainDude-y5m
top_comments.text: $200B capex, slipping timelines, and a bus factor meltdown. To me, this isn't a market dip. It's reward hacking at scale: optimize for valuation, lose the architects.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Feels less like a normal downturn and more like chasing the scoreboard. Pour money in, push dates, and watch the people who actually knew how things fit together walk out. You get great headlines but a fragile product underneath. Do you think leadership can course-correct now, or did they already trade long-term stability for short-term hype?

top_comments.author: @JordanJordi-d4d
top_comments.text: Jeff Dean practically wrote the playbook for large-scale ML infrastructure at Google. $200B in capex doesn't replace institutional knowledge when the people holding it walk.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Exactly. $200B buys hardware, not the playbook. That institutional knowledge from people like Jeff Dean is what actually makes the infra work. Lose the people, and you’re just paying to relearn everything. Can anyone catch up that fast, or is the knowledge gap the real moat?
